reason: internal/cli/version.go is generated and carries the generator's default literal (1.0.0); a reprint resets it. The literal has been bumped in place with a PATCH marker at every release since 2.0.0 so that a regeneration fails closed rather than silently shipping 1.0.0. 2.3.0 (2026-11-12: mva-status #30, recurring-gaps #31, the purchase duplicate guard #25, id and location on every create #26, mva-summary subtracting credit notes and checking itself against the ledger #24, missing-bilag reporting only what needs a bilag #28, doctor naming the company of each mirror finding #29 and reporting a newer release and what the installed skills require #32, log-event knowing the skill's operations #27) bumps the same literal again; this record replaces release-2-2-0 so the needle pins the current version, not a stale one. 2.2.0 was stamped in the tree on 2026-09-11 but its tag was never pushed, so 2.3.0 is the first GitHub release after 2.1.0 and carries everything in the 2.2.0 section as well. .goreleaser.yaml injects -X fiken-cli/internal/cli.version at release time, which matches this var; the Makefile injects nothing, so `make build`/`go install` binaries carry exactly this literal. The second goreleaser build (fiken-mcp) injects main.version, whose in-tree default in cmd/fiken-mcp/main.go stays 0.0.0-dev and is not touched here. CHANGELOG.md carries the 2.3.0 section above 2.2.0. Both skills state metadata.fiken-cli.requires 2.3.0, the version whose commands they describe; TestRepoSkillsStateTheirMinimumVersion fails if a skill names a version newer than this literal.
validated_outcome: make check green on the release commit; `fiken-cli version` prints 2.3.0 from a plain go build.
